prompt: It is a fact that there are a lot of languages in this world, but every year several of the languages just disappear. A group of people believe that the extinction of some languages is not a crucial problem since communication will be more effective with fewer languages.To what extent do you agree or disagree.
essay:
Language plays an essential role in our lives because it allows people to communicate and preserve their culture and identity. Although some people argue that the disappearance of languages is not a serious problem because fewer languages could make communication easier, I largely disagree with this view. I believe that linguistic diversity should be protected while people can also learn a common language for international communication.

Firstly, the loss of a language can result in the loss of valuable cultural knowledge. Traditional stories, local knowledge and family history are often passed from one generation to another through language. If younger people stop using their home language, they may gradually lose their connection with older family members and their cultural background. For example, when a small community moves to a large city, young people may use the dominant language at school and work and eventually stop speaking their home language with their families.

Furthermore, a language naturally changes over time, but this is different from its complete disappearance. New words and expressions may replace older ones, allowing communication to develop while the language remains alive. Therefore, language development should not be confused with language extinction.

However, I acknowledge that learning a common international language can make communication more effective. English, for instance, is widely used in business, education and travel. People can use it to communicate internationally while continuing to speak their own language at home.

In conclusion, I largely disagree that the disappearance of languages is an insignificant issue. Although a common language can reduce communication barriers, preserving different languages is essential for protecting cultural knowledge and family connections. The best approach is therefore to learn a common international language without abandoning native languages.
